start_here: Say to your AI: "Show me where each phrase of this piece came from." It runs tool:show-where-each-phrase-came-from with piece set to that piece's id and credential_name set to the name you hold your database connection under.

lists.label: Piece provenance
lists.holds: One row per phrase of a made piece: the span it sits in, the library row it came from, its quote and when it was recorded.

values.quote: an example phrase from the source
a second example phrase from the source

alike: a source sheet beside a draft
citations in a research notes list

instructions: 1. Hold your database's connection string in your vault under a name of your choosing, such as my-database-connection. The string is never typed into a request.
2. Say which piece you want in plain words. Your AI calls tools:run with tool tool:show-where-each-phrase-came-from, piece (the piece id) and credential_name.
3. Read the answer: piece_id, columns, rows and row_count. Each row is one phrase, matching list:piece-provenance.
4. The page at /where-it-came-from shows the same rows for the piece in its surface input.

worked_examples.title: Where each phrase of one made piece came from
worked_examples.ask: Show me where each phrase of this piece came from.
worked_examples.hands_back: row_count 2 and two rows, for example span "slide-1" with quote "an example phrase from the source".

pour.how: Pour the two example rows into a provenance list the person already keeps, mapping the same fields; this tool changes neither list.
